items.q: Match the following metabolic syndrome criterion to the cutoff (per source/standard) — 1) Waist circumference (men) 2) Triglycerides 3) HDL (men) 4) BP … A) ≥90 cm (Asian Indian) B) ≥150 mg/dL C) <40 mg/dL D) ≥130/85 mmHg
items.exp: Asian-Indian waist circumference cut-off for men is ≥90 cm; triglycerides ≥150 mg/dL; HDL <40 mg/dL in men; BP ≥130/85 mmHg. (Book p922)

items.q: A 50-year-old South Asian man has BP 132/86 mmHg, fasting TG 165 mg/dL, HDL 38 mg/dL and waist circumference 95 cm. The diagnostic label is:
items.exp: Three of five criteria (waist, TG, HDL, BP) are met; this is metabolic syndrome. (Book p922)

items.q: Assess BMI categories: I Asian-Indian overweight is BMI ≥23. II Obesity is BMI ≥25 in Asian-Indian classification.
items.exp: Asian-Indian BMI thresholds: overweight ≥23, obesity ≥25 (compared with WHO ≥25 and ≥30). (Book p922)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among metabolic syndrome criteria?
items.exp: Fasting glucose is a metabolic syndrome criterion in NCEP-ATP III but not in IDF's primary central obesity definition; waist is central to IDF criteria. (Book p922)

items.q: The page's Asian-Indian BMI cut-off for overweight is ___.
items.exp: Asian-Indian cut-offs: normal <23, overweight ≥23, obese ≥25 (with morbid obesity at higher values). (Book p922)

items.q: Match the following milestone in T2DM history — 1) First clinical use 2) Role of UKPDS 3) Discovery … A) 1921 insulin (later refined for type 2) B) Demonstrated benefit of glycaemic control C) Insulin by Banting and Best
items.exp: Insulin was discovered in 1921; first clinical use came shortly after; UKPDS established benefit of glycaemic control in T2DM. (Book p922)

items.q: A 50-year-old with BMI 26, BP 138/88, TG 178 mg/dL, HDL 36 mg/dL and FPG 102 mg/dL asks about diabetes risk. The most consistent label is:
items.exp: Metabolic syndrome is present; FPG 100–125 places the patient in the pre-diabetes range. (Book p922)

items.q: Assess waist cut-offs: I Asian-Indian women use a lower waist cut-off than men. II IDF uses the same Asian waist cut-off for men and women.
items.exp: Asian women use ≥80 cm (vs ≥90 cm men); IDF uses the same Asian-specific cut-off for both sexes but is sex-specific. (Book p922)

items.q: Match the following to its discovery timeline — 1) Insulin 2) Sulfonylureas 3) Metformin 4) GLP-1 agonist … A) 1921 B) 1940s–50s C) 1950s (biguanides) D) 2005 onwards
items.exp: Insulin 1921; sulfonylureas mid-20th century; metformin (biguanides) widely adopted mid-century; GLP-1 agonists from 2005. (Book p922)

items.q: An Asian-Indian patient with BMI 27 has BP 128/82, TG 145 mg/dL, HDL 42 mg/dL and FPG 92 mg/dL. The patient meets:
items.exp: BMI 27 exceeds the Asian-Indian obesity cut-off ≥25 and waist typically ≥90 cm; BP, TG and HDL do not meet criteria. (Book p922)

items.q: The metabolic syndrome criterion for fasting plasma glucose is ≥ ___ mg/dL.
items.exp: Fasting plasma glucose ≥100 mg/dL (or treatment) is one of the metabolic syndrome criteria. (Book p922)

items.q: Assess these facts: I South Asians have higher diabetes risk at lower BMIs. II Metabolic syndrome increases cardiovascular risk beyond its components.
items.exp: South Asians have higher risk at lower BMIs (the basis of Asian-Indian cut-offs); metabolic syndrome increases CV risk beyond individual components. (Book p922)
